summary: Track B worker wave: Haiku reconstructs planned batches, Sonnet spot-verifies, Haiku fixes once

layout_requests: Carried forward from the earlier ledger notes, not re-verified in this fix pass: vox-audio sound_manager.hpp declares nativeResumeSoundBig (0x5314c8) and nativeStopSoundBig (0x531570) as int; the binary's calls are void. nativeSetVolumeBig (0x53177c) is declared int with channel as the third argument; it should be void. nativeStopAllBigSound (0x531940) is declared with a second fade_ms argument and an int return; the body reads only its first argument. No new request for nativeSetVolume (0x53170c) or nativeSetPitch (0x53183c): vox-audio does not declare either, and IDA xrefs_to shows no code caller, only one data xref each (0x31618 and 0x4d578, JNI table entries).

NVThreadInit: tinyxml-and-c-libs/include/tinyxml-and-c-libs/nvthread.hpp and src/nvthread.cpp take and store an int. JNI_OnLoad passes the JavaVM pointer through it, so the pointer is truncated on a 64-bit host. Change the parameter to a pointer type in both files and drop the static_cast in JNI_OnLoad (src/p1-core-platform-global-f216b6-2.cpp).

game-app/src/g1-game-app-GSInit-78f1fa-0.cpp declares extern C void nativeLoadMovie(const char*, int). The binary returns the jint of loadMovie, and this batch defines it as int nativeLoadMovie(const char*, int). Make the GSInit declaration int.

game/include/dh2/global/menu_main_menu.hpp declares int nativeOpenIGP(int) with C++ linkage. This batch defines extern C void nativeOpenIGP(int) (the binary's symbol name, void because the Java side is void). Change the declaration to extern C void.
game/include/dh2/global/native_app_hud_level.hpp declares int nativeOpenGLive(int) with C++ linkage. This batch defines extern C void nativeOpenGLive(int). Change the declaration to extern C void.

NotifyTrophy(int) has no declaration in the game tree (game-items-save TrophyManager). This batch defines extern C void NotifyTrophy(int). Declare it that way. chunk_006.c (TrophyManager::UnlockTrophiesGLLive, 0x37fab4) returns this call's r0 as its own result, which has no defined value. The caller should not use it.

Width_Screen and Height_Screen (game-owned .data words, ELF 0x99b114 and 0x99b118, declared in game/include/dh2/global/screen_size.hpp) have no definition in the tree. This batch's DungeonHunter2.nativeSetPhone writes them and the test defines them. The game globals batch must define them.

Globals defined elsewhere that this batch reads: mEnv, mClassGLMediaPlayer and the GLMediaPlayer sound IDs (p1-core-platform-global-f216b6-0 and -1), mClassDungeonHunter2 and the mMethodVZ* IDs (p1-tinyxml-and-c-libs-global-f216b6-0). This batch sets them but does not redefine them. Its own new globals are in src/p1-core-platform-global-f216b6-2.cpp and declared in tb/android_jni_platform.hpp.

game/include/dh2/global/native_app_hud_level.hpp line 21 declares int nativeIsSupportMM() with C++ linkage. The definition in core-platform/src/p1-core-platform-global-f216b6-3.cpp is extern "C" (the binary's plain symbol). Change the declaration to extern "C" int nativeIsSupportMM(); so game-app callers link (same fix as nativeOpenGLive, batch -2).

Integrator: the app-event functions appPause (int), appResume (float), appKeyReleased (MenuManager*, int), appKeyPressed (int), appTrackBall (void) and appOnTouch (int, 8 int words) are declared in core-platform/include/core-platform/tb/android_jni_app_events.hpp from their call sites. Check them against their definitions when the app and menu batches are ledgered (IDA: appKeyReleased returns MenuManager*, appResume returns float).

Globals defined in this batch's source (one definition each, not in game-app/src/Globals.cpp): mTimeCallbackFinished = 1, Orientation = 1, Enable_Orientation = 1 (.data words, values read from the binary), Touch_Hack_int = 0 (.bss), and the Musicplayer class and method IDs (mClassMusicplayer, mMethodGetNumPlaylists, mMethodGetPlaylistName, mMethodSetPlaylist, mMethodPlayBGMusic, mMethodnativeChangeStep, mMethodResumeMusicBG, mMethodPauseMusicBG, mMethodStopMusicBG, mMethodGetisplaying). Keep these here when the globals batch is merged.

Declarations for game-app rows 0x324210 (Application::OnInterruptPause) and 0x417fe8 (GS_InterruptLoading::Dtor): nativeGetisplaying and nativePauseMusicBG are now declared with C linkage in core-platform/include/core-platform/tb/android_jni_musicplayer.hpp. Those partial rows can include that header and call the natives. nativePauseMusicBG is declared void, because the binary's int is the r0 left by a void JNI call; a caller that reads its return value needs review.

vox-audio skip rows 0x369480, 0x369484, 0x36c734 and 0x36cda8 (VoxSoundManager playlist and iPod control) can now call the declared natives: nativeGetNumPlaylists (int), nativeGetPlaylistName(int) returning char* (malloc'd, never freed, as in the binary), nativePlayBGMusic (void) and nativeGetisplaying (int, returns 0).

VoxEngine::GetEmitterHandles facade returns void (include/vox-audio/vox/voxengine.hpp:119, src/voxengine.cpp:597) but the binary returns the int count from VoxEngineInternal::GetEmitterHandles. Making the facade return int unlocks the count-driven parts of SetMusicState, IsSoundPlaying, IsMusicPlaying, Stop, Stop3D and Resume.
Arrays::Sounds::members (pydata, 12-byte records, sound data index at +4) needs a accessor that vox-audio can reach. Five partials (SetMusicState, IsMusicPlaying, Stop, Stop3D, Resume) wait on it.

The VoxSoundManager constructor (0x36c7b0, ledger row skipped) must set engine_ from VoxEngine::GetVoxEngine(), allocate sounds_ with sound_count_ entries and load sound_pack_. Until it lands, StopAllSounds, PauseAllSounds and ResumeAllSounds do nothing (engine_ null) and LoadSound writes through a null sounds_.

The native bridge bodies in core-platform (rows 0x531570, 0x5314c8, 0x531940, 0x53177c, 0x531a64) must match the extern "C" declarations in sound_manager.hpp. nativeStopAllBigSound is declared with two arguments because every call site passes the fade; its body reads only the first.
Point3D<float> has no type in the port. Stop3D takes const float* (x, y, z), matching how the body indexes it.
VoxMemHint names only kVoxMemHintDefault (0). LoadSound passes MemoryHintState 4 by cast, from the operator new(uint, MemoryHintState) call in the listing.

Global types declared extern in sound_manager.hpp: JAVA_SOUNDS and Resume_Sound_Interrupt bool, Save_Current_Music_ID int, music_volume and sfx_vfx_volume float (inferred: the listing stores the float register with no conversion), RES_PATH const char*. The globals batches must define them with these types.

Standalone check of tests/sound_manager_test.cpp with check_tu --test now fails to link: VoxSoundManager embeds VoxSoundPackXML at +0x64, so its destructor is needed, and the sound-pack loader needs more sources. The CMake test target links dh2_all, so the real build is unaffected.

mEnv has one definition in the image: port/decomp-reconstruction/core-platform/src/p1-core-platform-global-f216b6-0.cpp line 16. Other batches must use the extern from tinyxml-and-c-libs/include/tinyxml-and-c-libs/jni_globals.hpp or core-platform/include/core-platform/tb/android_jni_bridge.hpp and must not define it. The tinyxml-and-c-libs test defines a test-only mEnv because it links only its own batch source.
The other mClassDungeonHunter2 and mMethodVZ* globals stay defined in tinyxml-and-c-libs/src/p1-tinyxml-and-c-libs-global-f216b6-0.cpp, with no second definition.
